all_found.desc: [BUG] When a run on branch B re-raises a fingerprint already open for the same target, Reconcile moves the row's GitHead to B's head but keeps Branch set to the original branch A, and the activeExisting dedup stops a row for B from being written. With A still live, rebasing or amending B moves the recorded head out of B's range; Classify("A", head) then returns OtherBranch on B, so B's pr-ready/epic-ready stop blocking on an obligation B's own task-done re-raised — a rewrite silently clears B's gate.

[BUG] The back-on-branch-a half of AC-4.1 and both AC-4.3 checks pass even if the ledger never blocks, because branch-a's committed NEEDS_REVISION task-done log is in its diff and yields 'Blocked targets: t-a' on its own; the findings unit tests have no rebase or amend case. A regression that drops a branch's own ledger findings after rebase or amend — the property AC-4.3 exists to protect — goes undetected (verified by mutant: ScopedBlocking putting every blocker elsewhere keeps these tests green).

[ADVISORY] The CLI-level AC-4.6 test passes with the fix reverted, because branch-a's merged log makes the projection treat its ledger blocker as historical anyway. A PR naming this test as AC-4.6 proof overstates coverage; only the ledger-level test fails under a revert.

[ADVISORY] The advisory line says the out-of-scope blockers 'block that branch', but the count includes orphaned rows (merged-and-deleted branches, out-of-range legacy rows) that block nothing. A reader looks for a live branch that an orphaned finding supposedly gates.

[ADVISORY] A pre-#178 binary that rewrites the ledger drops the unknown branch field, silently turning rows back into legacy rows. Mixing binaries in one checkout loses branch ownership, and a row can reappear as a blocker on a sibling branch via the legacy rule; tracked with version-skew hardening (#180).

[BUG] Raising an open finding again on another branch moves the single ledger row's Branch and GitHead to that branch, so the branch that first raised it — which still contains the defect — no longer owns it. Stacked flow: blocker F raised on branch-a; `git switch -c branch-b`, commit, task-done again re-raises F and the row becomes branch-b's; back on branch-a ScopedBlocking returns in=0 (OtherBranch), so branch-a's pr-ready passes and it merges with F unfixed. A throwaway branch (re-review on tmp, delete tmp, amend branch-a) orphans it the same way. Reproduced at 1348de8.

[ADVISORY] The re-raise branch handling only applies to status open, so an override-pending blocker re-raised on another branch keeps its original branch and the activeExisting dedup writes no row for the new branch. Work moved to an unrelated branch B (cherry-picked) re-raises a pending-override blocker; the row stays on live branch A, so B's pr-ready passes though the pending override should keep blocking.

[ADVISORY] prReadyBlocksTA searches for t-a anywhere after the first 'Blocked targets: ' rather than only in that line's comma-separated list. If branch-a is blocked by another target, the positive assertions can pass while t-a's own ledger finding no longer blocks.

[BUG] The fix transition requires owns() (name leg only), while ScopedBlocking also puts rows in scope by the range leg, so a branch cut from the branch that raised a finding (a fix branch, a stacked branch, or one a lower branch was fast-forward-merged into) is blocked by that row and its --previous-run fix chain can never close it. Record a finding on feat (run mrv-a); `git switch -c feat-fix`, commit the fix, Reconcile with PreviousRunIDs=[mrv-a] and no findings: the row stays open and in scope on feat-fix, which stays NEEDS_REVISION until ESCALATED — override is the only way out. Verified at f6d4377.

[BUG] owns() gives every branch ownership of branchless rows (pre-#178 legacy rows, detached-HEAD rows), so a re-raise on any branch refreshes such a row in place and re-stamps it with that branch's name and head. A legacy (or detached) blocker in scope on branch-a: `git switch -c tmp`, commit, re-review → the row becomes tmp's; on branch-a it is now elsewhere, and after `git branch -D tmp` orphaned — branch-a's gates stop blocking on an unfixed defect, and branch-a's own fix chain can no longer close it either. Every legacy blocker in an upgraded ledger can be cleared this way. Verified at f6d4377.

[BUG] A ledger finding stops blocking its own work after routine commands: `git switch -c branch-a2`, `git branch -D branch-a`, `git commit --amend` — its branch is gone and its head left the range, and Classify skips the past-heads leg for a named row, so it is Orphaned. pr-ready on branch-a2 no longer blocks on t-a (only 'Open on other branches'); before #178 the same sequence still blocked. Verified in a scratch clone at 66ed45a.

[BUG] The detached-run refresh leg re-stamps the GitHead of every branchless row for the target, including rows that do not gate the detached HEAD. A legacy blocker reachable from branch-a, re-raised by a task-done on a detached HEAD cut from main, gets that detached head; back on branch-a it is unreachable and elsewhere, so branch-a's gate clears without a fix. Verified in a scratch clone.

[ADVISORY] A pre-#178 branchless row is never moved forward by a named run, so it stays at its pre-upgrade head and relies on the legacy reachability/reflog rule. After a rebase and reflog expiry, or delete-and-recreate of the branch, it becomes Orphaned and stops blocking until re-raised.

[ADVISORY] supersedesFreshness and supersedeLegacyContextRisk still act on every row for the target whatever branch recorded it. A task-done on branch B can supersede branch A's open mutation-freshness row for the same task.
[ADVISORY] prReadyBlocksTA's comment says 'exactly the target t-a' but the body is a contains check. The comment overstates the assertion.

[ADVISORY] No test pins that a named run dedupes against an in-scope branchless row; the mutant dropping that leg passes the suite. A regression writing a duplicate named row next to every legacy row would pass CI.

[ADVISORY] The 'orphaned row closable by a chain' assertion is vacuous (the tmp row is in range, InScope); a mutant restricting the fix transition to blocksHere survives. Rows from deleted branches could become permanently unclosable without CI noticing.

[BUG] A detached-HEAD run does not dedupe against a named row that gates it, so re-raising a finding at the branch's own head (git checkout --detach, task-done) writes a second, branchless row for the same fingerprint and target. The verdict counts two blockers; back on the branch its --previous-run chain closes its own row but the branchless duplicate (in range) stays open and blocks until a chain names the detached run. At 985b8d9 the same sequence deduped. Verified in a scratch repo.

[BUG] A named run that re-raises a finding deduplicates against a branchless row that gates it but never refreshes it, so a branchless row from a detached review at a commit that is not one of the branch's reflog heads is orphaned by a routine `git rebase main`, and the branch holds no row of its own. detach, commit D1, task-done (branchless row); commit D2, `git switch -c feat`, commit, task-done (deduped); advance main, `git rebase main` on feat: ScopedBlocking in-scope is empty and feat's pr-ready no longer blocks on a finding feat itself raised. Verified in a scratch clone.

[ADVISORY] The branch is read at Reconcile time while GitHead was captured at run start, so a git switch mid-run can pair branch B with a head of A. Over-blocks the switched-to branch; never fails open.

[BUG] A detached run refreshes a gating branchless row's GitHead to the detached head, so a review on a throwaway detached commit moves the only row for feat's blocker off feat's history. feat: detach + review (branchless row R at feat's tip); switch feat + review (dedupes onto R); detach, commit scratch, review again (R moves to scratch); on feat ScopedBlocking in=[] — feat's unfixed blocker stops gating pr-ready. Verified in a scratch clone at d1418d0.
[ADVISORY] With a partially read scope (Current set, known false) after a rename, the dedupe takes neither the detached nor the name leg. A duplicate row beside the former-name row; over-count only.

[BUG] When the scope is unknown but the branch name was read (a later Load git call failed), the refresh `mine(record) || !sc.Known()` re-stamps every same-target open row — including another live branch's — with this branch's name and head. branch-a records F; a review on branch-b re-raising F while a scope git call times out rewrites the row to branch-b; back on branch-a with a readable scope ScopedBlocking returns in=[] — a transient git failure fails open. Verified in scratch clones at 806eb42.

[ADVISORY] A legacy override-pending row not in the branch's reflog does not absorb a re-raise; only granted rows do. A later grant of the legacy override leaves a duplicate open row needing a second grant or chain.

[ADVISORY] task-done on main over uncommitted work, then `git switch -c feat` and commit: the finding stays recorded on live main at feat's fork point, so it does not block feat. feat's gates stop gating the defect in its own work unless re-reviewed (the accepted 'recorded on main' rule, with moved work).

findings.issue_text: [BUG] With a partly read scope (branch name read, a later Load call failed), the dedupe's !sc.Known() leg folds this branch's re-raise into another branch's row, so this branch never gets a row of its own. branch-a records F; branch-b re-raises F under a partly read scope; the ledger keeps only branch-a's row; once git recovers ScopedBlocking on branch-b gives in=[] — one transient git failure leaves branch-b's pr-ready unblocked by a defect it contains. Verified in a scratch clone at a94e09c.

[ADVISORY] The comment and ARCHITECTURE say the fallback refresh runs only outside a repository, but `!sc.Known() && branch == ""` also holds on a detached HEAD after a scope git failure. Docs overstate the guarantee (a transient git failure on a detached review can move rows).

[ADVISORY] The comment says all scope git calls run before the ledger is read, but blocksHere's legacy reachability check runs inside the dedupe loop, for fingerprints this run did not even raise. Extra git calls stretch the unlocked read-modify-write (#180); the comment misleads.

[ADVISORY] Pre-#178 Reconcile moved a row's gitHead to whichever branch last re-raised it, so an upgraded legacy row first raised on A and last on B carries B's head and reads as Orphaned on A. A's pr-ready stops blocking on it until A's task-done re-raises it.
[ADVISORY] No test pins the `&& branch == ""` guard on the fallback refresh; the mutant dropping it survives. A revert would let a partly read scope move a branchless row off the branch it gates.

rejected.desc: [BUG] Scoping findings.UnresolvedBlocking by branch also narrows epic-ready's childOpenBlockerLogs, whose job is to surface open ledger blockers of the epic's child tasks, which are usually recorded on the children's own branches. After a child branch is squash- or rebase-merged into the epic branch (kept or deleted), the child's recorded head is outside the epic's range and its open blocker classifies other-branch/orphaned, so epic-ready passes with a child task still NEEDS_REVISION and logs nothing about it.

[ADVISORY] The in-scope blockers are filtered by InViewScope(options.MutationViews) but the elsewhere slice counted into 'Open on other branches: N' is not. A view-restricted run overstates the other-branch count; cosmetic, the verdict is unchanged.

[ADVISORY] currentBranch runs the whole scope.Load (symbolic-ref, remote, for-each-ref, fork point, rev-list of the range, reflog) on every Reconcile just to read Scope.Current, and pr-ready loads the scope twice (ScopedBlocking, then Reconcile). Several extra git calls per gate run, each with a 20s timeout; latency only, no correctness failure.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] pr-ready reads blockers through the branch scope while epic-ready reads child blockers across branches, so on an epic branch a squash-merged-and-deleted child branch's open ledger finding no longer blocks pr-ready. The pre-merge pr-ready gate is weaker than epic-ready for the same child obligation unless epic-ready is run first.

[ADVISORY] findings calls git itself through a package-private loadScope seam instead of taking the caller's injected GitRunner. Hermetic caller tests (prready, epicready) silently run real git on their temp root, and the stamped branch can differ from the branch the caller's seam reported.

[ADVISORY] RenderIndexWithRecords still renders the blocker section of docs/metareview/FINDINGS.md from the whole ledger, unscoped. A run on branch-b commits branch-a's open findings into branch-b's FINDINGS.md as unresolved blockers; no gate reads it, but the audit trail contradicts the pr-ready log.

[ADVISORY] The ledger-only AC-4.1/4.3 tests still pass when new findings record no branch, because the legacy rule (past heads, reachability, range) keeps such rows in scope in exactly these scenarios. A regression in branch recording is caught only by the unit assertion in TestReconcileRecordsTheBranch; no integration case needs the name leg (e.g. a recorded head git no longer has).

rejected.desc: [BUG] Reconcile's returned OpenFindings/OpenBlockingCount (openForRun) and Findings (activeCurrent) still filter by target only, so another live branch's open row for the same task/epic target counts in this branch's task-done/epic-ready verdict. Task t blocked on branch-a; a clean task-done of t on branch-b (or branch-b's own fixed chain) still returns OpenBlockingCount=1 from branch-a's row, so branch-b stays NEEDS_REVISION then ESCALATED on a finding it cannot close. Verified at f6d4377.

[BUG] Under one row per branch, a row written on a throwaway branch that is then deleted can only be closed by a run on that branch name, yet epic-ready reads child blockers from every branch, so the orphaned row blocks the child's epic-ready forever. tmp re-raises task t's finding and is deleted; t's own branch fixes its row; epic-ready over t stays NEEDS_REVISION from the orphaned tmp row, and chaining --previous-run to tmp's run from a live branch does not close it.

[ADVISORY] Scope.Owns duplicates Classify's name-leg predicate instead of Classify calling Owns. A later change to one copy only makes Reconcile's ownership and ScopedBlocking's classification disagree.

[ADVISORY] Run.Branch is an exported override no production caller sets, and when set to something other than the checked-out branch owns() silently drops the former-name leg while judging rows against the checkout's scope. A future caller passing an explicit branch gets mixed semantics (duplicate rows after a rename).
[ADVISORY] No test covers ElsewhereBlockers on pr-ready's reused-verdict path. Dropping it there would silently remove the advisory from reused logs without failing CI.

The epic's task-done passes but epic-ready keeps blocking on the child forever from the epic branch; before #178 the chain closed it. Verified at 66ed45a.

[ADVISORY] Epic-ready's across-branches read counts an abandoned branch's copy of a child's row as the child's obligation while that branch exists. A child redone on a new branch and fixed there still blocks epic-ready through the old branch's row until the old branch is deleted and a chain names it.

[ADVISORY] The 'Open on other branches' count includes orphaned rows, which stay open forever unless a chain or override closes them. Every pr-ready log carries a growing non-actionable advisory and ScopedBlocking never takes its no-blockers fast path.

[ADVISORY] Legacy-head reachability checks can trigger promisor lazy fetches in a partial clone; scope's git runner does not set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. A local gate makes network fetches per pruned legacy head, adding latency or 20s timeouts.

[ADVISORY] Each distinct legacy head costs its own 20s-timeout git calls with no early stop after a stall, and pr-ready loads the scope twice. A stalled git with many legacy heads can hold a gate for minutes before failing closed.

[ADVISORY] When scope.Load cannot read the branch, ScopedBlocking fails closed but nothing in the pr-ready log says branch scoping was skipped (#171 P8 'say why'). A git timeout makes branch-b block on branch-a's findings again with no explanation.

[ADVISORY] reviewlog.Discover still sets a log's HasUnresolvedBlockers from the whole ledger by run id, branch-blind. A visible (e.g. uncommitted) review log of branch A can still read as blocking on B while pr-ready reports it only as open elsewhere.
[ADVISORY] The exported UnresolvedBlocking kept its name but became branch-scoped. A future caller expecting every blocker silently gets only this branch's.

[ADVISORY] The elsewhere count includes other branches' pr-ready 'Unresolved review blockers' summary rows alongside the blockers they summarise. The Repository Health Advisory overstates the count (report only).
[ADVISORY] The blocksHere guard on the freshness-supersede transition has no test; removing it survives the suite. A revert would let another branch's run supersede a stale-mutation blocker silently.

findings.consequence: After a child branch is squash- or rebase-merged into the epic branch (kept or deleted), the child's recorded head is outside the epic's range and its open blocker classifies other-branch/orphaned, so epic-ready passes with a child task still NEEDS_REVISION and logs nothing about it.

findings.consequence: A regression that drops a branch's own ledger findings after rebase or amend — the property AC-4.3 exists to protect — goes undetected (verified by mutant: ScopedBlocking putting every blocker elsewhere keeps these tests green).

findings.consequence: A PR naming this test as AC-4.6 proof overstates coverage; only the ledger-level test fails under a revert.

findings.consequence: A view-restricted run overstates the other-branch count; cosmetic, the verdict is unchanged.

findings.consequence: A reader looks for a live branch that an orphaned finding supposedly gates.

findings.consequence: Several extra git calls per gate run, each with a 20s timeout; latency only, no correctness failure.

findings.consequence: Work moved to an unrelated branch B (cherry-picked) re-raises a pending-override blocker; the row stays on live branch A, so B's pr-ready passes though the pending override should keep blocking.

findings.consequence: A local gate makes network fetches per pruned legacy head, adding latency or 20s timeouts.

findings.consequence: A stalled git with many legacy heads can hold a gate for minutes before failing closed.

findings.consequence: A task-done on branch B can supersede branch A's open mutation-freshness row for the same task.

findings.consequence: A single git stall strands an extra blocking row the branch's normal chain does not close.
findings.issue: When symbolic-ref fails (timeout, git missing), Current is empty on a named branch, so the run behaves as detached and writes branchless duplicate rows.

findings.consequence: A git timeout makes branch-b block on branch-a's findings again with no explanation.

findings.consequence: A visible (e.g. uncommitted) review log of branch A can still read as blocking on B while pr-ready reports it only as open elsewhere.
findings.issue: reviewlog.Discover still sets a log's HasUnresolvedBlockers from the whole ledger by run id, branch-blind.

findings.consequence: A future caller expecting every blocker silently gets only this branch's.
findings.issue: The exported UnresolvedBlocking kept its name but became branch-scoped.

findings.consequence: The Repository Health Advisory overstates the count (report only).
findings.issue: The elsewhere count includes other branches' pr-ready 'Unresolved review blockers' summary rows alongside the blockers they summarise.

findings.consequence: A revert would let another branch's run supersede a stale-mutation blocker silently.
findings.issue: The blocksHere guard on the freshness-supersede transition has no test; removing it survives the suite.

Verified in a scratch clone.
findings.issue: A named run that re-raises a finding deduplicates against a branchless row that gates it but never refreshes it, so a branchless row from a detached review at a commit that is not one of the branch's reflog heads is orphaned by a routine `git rebase main`, and the branch holds no row of its own.

findings.consequence: The stacked branch blocks until a second request+grant; before #178 the overridden row deduped the re-raise.
findings.issue: The dedupe guard skips a granted-override row another branch recorded, so a stacked branch re-raising the same finding gets a new open row although a human already granted an exception for it on the lower branch.

findings.consequence: A user seeing the advisory or a finding stop blocking after git switch finds no explanation in the command docs.
findings.issue: The user-facing pr-ready docs (skills/review-pr-ready/SKILL.md, commands/review-pr-ready.md) do not mention branch-scoped findings or the 'Open on other branches: N' advisory.

findings.consequence: Two concurrent gates in one checkout are more likely to lose an update.
findings.issue: Reconcile loads the scope (several git calls) between reading and writing the unlocked ledger, widening the read-modify-write window.

findings.consequence: Over-blocks the switched-to branch; never fails open.
findings.issue: The branch is read at Reconcile time while GitHead was captured at run start, so a git switch mid-run can pair branch B with a head of A.

findings.consequence: Inflated counts and duplicate log lines; verdict unchanged.
findings.issue: A stacked branch re-raising a finding open on its lower branch lists the fingerprint twice in OpenFindings.

findings.consequence: Dropping it later would not fail CI.
findings.issue: Nothing tests that scope.RealRunner passes GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1.

findings.consequence: feat: detach + review (branchless row R at feat's tip); switch feat + review (dedupes onto R); detach, commit scratch, review again (R moves to scratch); on feat ScopedBlocking in=[] — feat's unfixed blocker stops gating pr-ready. Verified in a scratch clone at d1418d0.
findings.issue: A detached run refreshes a gating branchless row's GitHead to the detached head, so a review on a throwaway detached commit moves the only row for feat's blocker off feat's history.

findings.consequence: Docs and log text disagree; users look for a live owner of merged-and-deleted leftovers.
findings.issue: The pr-ready docs say the 'Open on other branches' findings still block their own branch, but the count also holds orphaned rows that block nothing.

findings.consequence: A later change can update one and not the other.
findings.issue: The refresh and dedupe ownership rules are inline compound booleans rather than named helpers tested as a pair.

findings.consequence: Fixes the dependency direction between the ledger and the FSM engine (tracked by mr-trz: move the git runner to a leaf package).
findings.issue: findings now imports internal/scope, which pulls in fsm/gate, fsm/run, fsm/converge and gitcontext.

findings.consequence: A duplicate row beside the former-name row; over-count only.
findings.issue: With a partially read scope (Current set, known false) after a rename, the dedupe takes neither the detached nor the name leg.

findings.consequence: In such containers branch scoping silently does nothing (fails closed, as #177 already does).
findings.issue: scope's hardened runner drops GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and system config, so safe.directory set only there makes scope unreadable while the review's other git calls succeed.

findings.consequence: branch-a records F; a review on branch-b re-raising F while a scope git call times out rewrites the row to branch-b; back on branch-a with a readable scope ScopedBlocking returns in=[] — a transient git failure fails open. Verified in scratch clones at 806eb42.
findings.issue: When the scope is unknown but the branch name was read (a later Load git call failed), the refresh `mine(record) || !sc.Known()` re-stamps every same-target open row — including another live branch's — with this branch's name and head.

findings.consequence: Doc disagrees with the code in an edge case.
findings.issue: ARCHITECTURE says no run moves a branchless row, but the unknown-scope fallback refreshes every row.

findings.consequence: A later grant of the legacy override leaves a duplicate open row needing a second grant or chain.
findings.issue: A legacy override-pending row not in the branch's reflog does not absorb a re-raise; only granted rows do.

findings.consequence: A regression in the Orphaned path would go unnoticed for the common merge.
findings.issue: AC-4.6 is proven only for merge --no-ff + delete; no test covers a squash-merged, deleted branch (this repository's merge style).

findings.consequence: feat's gates stop gating the defect in its own work unless re-reviewed (the accepted 'recorded on main' rule, with moved work).
findings.issue: task-done on main over uncommitted work, then `git switch -c feat` and commit: the finding stays recorded on live main at feat's fork point, so it does not block feat.

findings.consequence: A revert would write duplicate open rows unnoticed.
findings.issue: The unknown-scope dedupe leg has no test that fails when it is removed.

fix@0.summary: Re-raised findings now move to the raising branch with their head; epic-ready reads child blockers across branches; AC-4.1/4.3 proven via the ledger alone (new ledger-only CLI test + findings rebase/amend/rename test); advisory wording/view filter fixed; mixed-binary limitation documented (#180).

fix@1.summary: One ledger row per branch: Reconcile refreshes/dedupes/fixes only rows the run's branch owns (name, former name via scope.Owns, branchless), so a re-raise on a stacked/throwaway branch or of an override-pending row gives that branch its own row and never takes the first branch's. Test helper blockedTargets parses only the target list (test-only precision fix; no behavioral proof applies).

fix@2.summary: Reconcile: refresh only name-owned rows (scope.Owns) and never re-stamp branchless rows from a named run; verdict (OpenFindings/Findings) filtered to rows that gate this branch (Classify); --previous-run chain closes any named row unless another live branch owns it. Classify uses Owns; Run.Branch removed. Reused pr-ready path's other-branch advisory now tested.

fix@3.summary: Detached refresh guarded by blocksHere; --previous-run chain closes any row it names (pre-#178 repair path); freshness supersede only for rows gating this branch; GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH in scope runner; dedupe-against-legacy and orphaned-closable tests. The copy/delete/amend orphaning (b603482378df) is NOT changed in code: git state cannot distinguish it from a stacked branch whose merged parent was deleted (AC-4.6 / #177 TestAFastForwardedParentHeadStaysTheParents); it is documented as a known trade-off and filed as a follow-up.

fix@4.summary: Detached (or branch-unreadable) runs dedupe against every row that gates them; freshness-supersede guard pinned by TestFreshnessSupersedeOnlyForRowsThatGateTheRun.

fix@5.summary: Named runs dedupe against a branchless row only when its head is in the branch reflog (scope.PastHead), else record their own row; granted overrides that gate the branch absorb re-raises; scope loaded before ledger read; pr-ready docs. eb338a9bb809 (branch read at reconcile vs head at start) accepted: it only over-blocks, and gating on the reflog would break bare repos (no reflogs).

fix@6.summary: Only name-owned rows are refreshed (a branchless row is never moved); unknown scope refreshes and dedupes as before #178 (scope.Known); pr-ready doc wording for orphaned rows.

fix@7.summary: Refresh only name-owned rows (re-stamp only those); fallback refresh only when git cannot name the branch. Accepted, documented: 23fe131871be (a legacy override-pending row outside the reflog does not absorb re-raises — absorbing would reopen the orphaning path fixed earlier) and 084ecc2695e4 (uncommitted work reviewed on main then committed on a new branch stays main-recorded — the accepted recorded-on-main rule).

findings.issue: A pre-#178 branchless row is never moved forward by a named run, so it stays at its pre-upgrade head and relies on the legacy reachability/reflog rule.

findings.consequence: Every pr-ready log carries a growing non-actionable advisory and ScopedBlocking never takes its no-blockers fast path.
findings.issue: The 'Open on other branches' count includes orphaned rows, which stay open forever unless a chain or override closes them.

findings.consequence: A local gate makes network fetches per pruned legacy head, adding latency or 20s timeouts.
findings.issue: Legacy-head reachability checks can trigger promisor lazy fetches in a partial clone; scope's git runner does not set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH.

findings.consequence: A stalled git with many legacy heads can hold a gate for minutes before failing closed.
findings.issue: Each distinct legacy head costs its own 20s-timeout git calls with no early stop after a stall, and pr-ready loads the scope twice.

findings.consequence: A task-done on branch B can supersede branch A's open mutation-freshness row for the same task.
findings.issue: supersedesFreshness and supersedeLegacyContextRisk still act on every row for the target whatever branch recorded it.

findings.consequence: The comment overstates the assertion.
findings.issue: prReadyBlocksTA's comment says 'exactly the target t-a' but the body is a contains check.

findings.consequence: A regression writing a duplicate named row next to every legacy row would pass CI.
findings.issue: No test pins that a named run dedupes against an in-scope branchless row; the mutant dropping that leg passes the suite.

findings.consequence: Rows from deleted branches could become permanently unclosable without CI noticing.
findings.issue: The 'orphaned row closable by a chain' assertion is vacuous (the tmp row is in range, InScope); a mutant restricting the fix transition to blocksHere survives.

findings.consequence: The verdict counts two blockers; back on the branch its --previous-run chain closes its own row but the branchless duplicate (in range) stays open and blocks until a chain names the detached run. At 985b8d9 the same sequence deduped. Verified in a scratch repo.
findings.issue: A detached-HEAD run does not dedupe against a named row that gates it, so re-raising a finding at the branch's own head (git checkout --detach, task-done) writes a second, branchless row for the same fingerprint and target.

findings.consequence: A single git stall strands an extra blocking row the branch's normal chain does not close.
findings.issue: When symbolic-ref fails (timeout, git missing), Current is empty on a named branch, so the run behaves as detached and writes branchless duplicate rows.

findings.consequence: A git timeout makes branch-b block on branch-a's findings again with no explanation.
findings.issue: When scope.Load cannot read the branch, ScopedBlocking fails closed but nothing in the pr-ready log says branch scoping was skipped (#171 P8 'say why').

findings.consequence: A visible (e.g. uncommitted) review log of branch A can still read as blocking on B while pr-ready reports it only as open elsewhere.
findings.issue: reviewlog.Discover still sets a log's HasUnresolvedBlockers from the whole ledger by run id, branch-blind.

findings.consequence: A future caller expecting every blocker silently gets only this branch's.
findings.issue: The exported UnresolvedBlocking kept its name but became branch-scoped.

findings.consequence: The Repository Health Advisory overstates the count (report only).
findings.issue: The elsewhere count includes other branches' pr-ready 'Unresolved review blockers' summary rows alongside the blockers they summarise.

findings.consequence: A revert would let another branch's run supersede a stale-mutation blocker silently.
findings.issue: The blocksHere guard on the freshness-supersede transition has no test; removing it survives the suite.

findings.consequence: detach, commit D1, task-done (branchless row); commit D2, `git switch -c feat`, commit, task-done (deduped); advance main, `git rebase main` on feat: ScopedBlocking in-scope is empty and feat's pr-ready no longer blocks on a finding feat itself raised. Verified in a scratch clone.
findings.issue: A named run that re-raises a finding deduplicates against a branchless row that gates it but never refreshes it, so a branchless row from a detached review at a commit that is not one of the branch's reflog heads is orphaned by a routine `git rebase main`, and the branch holds no row of its own.

findings.consequence: The stacked branch blocks until a second request+grant; before #178 the overridden row deduped the re-raise.
findings.issue: The dedupe guard skips a granted-override row another branch recorded, so a stacked branch re-raising the same finding gets a new open row although a human already granted an exception for it on the lower branch.

findings.consequence: A user seeing the advisory or a finding stop blocking after git switch finds no explanation in the command docs.
findings.issue: The user-facing pr-ready docs (skills/review-pr-ready/SKILL.md, commands/review-pr-ready.md) do not mention branch-scoped findings or the 'Open on other branches: N' advisory.

findings.consequence: Two concurrent gates in one checkout are more likely to lose an update.
findings.issue: Reconcile loads the scope (several git calls) between reading and writing the unlocked ledger, widening the read-modify-write window.

findings.consequence: Over-blocks the switched-to branch; never fails open.
findings.issue: The branch is read at Reconcile time while GitHead was captured at run start, so a git switch mid-run can pair branch B with a head of A.

findings.consequence: Inflated counts and duplicate log lines; verdict unchanged.
findings.issue: A stacked branch re-raising a finding open on its lower branch lists the fingerprint twice in OpenFindings.

findings.consequence: Dropping it later would not fail CI.
findings.issue: Nothing tests that scope.RealRunner passes GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1.

findings.consequence: feat: detach + review (branchless row R at feat's tip); switch feat + review (dedupes onto R); detach, commit scratch, review again (R moves to scratch); on feat ScopedBlocking in=[] — feat's unfixed blocker stops gating pr-ready. Verified in a scratch clone at d1418d0.
findings.issue: A detached run refreshes a gating branchless row's GitHead to the detached head, so a review on a throwaway detached commit moves the only row for feat's blocker off feat's history.

findings.consequence: Docs and log text disagree; users look for a live owner of merged-and-deleted leftovers.
findings.issue: The pr-ready docs say the 'Open on other branches' findings still block their own branch, but the count also holds orphaned rows that block nothing.

findings.consequence: A later change can update one and not the other.
findings.issue: The refresh and dedupe ownership rules are inline compound booleans rather than named helpers tested as a pair.

findings.consequence: Fixes the dependency direction between the ledger and the FSM engine (tracked by mr-trz: move the git runner to a leaf package).
findings.issue: findings now imports internal/scope, which pulls in fsm/gate, fsm/run, fsm/converge and gitcontext.

findings.consequence: A duplicate row beside the former-name row; over-count only.
findings.issue: With a partially read scope (Current set, known false) after a rename, the dedupe takes neither the detached nor the name leg.

findings.consequence: In such containers branch scoping silently does nothing (fails closed, as #177 already does).
findings.issue: scope's hardened runner drops GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and system config, so safe.directory set only there makes scope unreadable while the review's other git calls succeed.

findings.consequence: branch-a records F; a review on branch-b re-raising F while a scope git call times out rewrites the row to branch-b; back on branch-a with a readable scope ScopedBlocking returns in=[] — a transient git failure fails open. Verified in scratch clones at 806eb42.
findings.issue: When the scope is unknown but the branch name was read (a later Load git call failed), the refresh `mine(record) || !sc.Known()` re-stamps every same-target open row — including another live branch's — with this branch's name and head.

findings.consequence: Doc disagrees with the code in an edge case.
findings.issue: ARCHITECTURE says no run moves a branchless row, but the unknown-scope fallback refreshes every row.

findings.consequence: A later grant of the legacy override leaves a duplicate open row needing a second grant or chain.
findings.issue: A legacy override-pending row not in the branch's reflog does not absorb a re-raise; only granted rows do.

findings.consequence: A regression in the Orphaned path would go unnoticed for the common merge.
findings.issue: AC-4.6 is proven only for merge --no-ff + delete; no test covers a squash-merged, deleted branch (this repository's merge style).

findings.consequence: feat's gates stop gating the defect in its own work unless re-reviewed (the accepted 'recorded on main' rule, with moved work).
findings.issue: task-done on main over uncommitted work, then `git switch -c feat` and commit: the finding stays recorded on live main at feat's fork point, so it does not block feat.

findings.consequence: A revert would write duplicate open rows unnoticed.
findings.issue: The unknown-scope dedupe leg has no test that fails when it is removed.

findings.consequence: branch-a records F; branch-b re-raises F under a partly read scope; the ledger keeps only branch-a's row; once git recovers ScopedBlocking on branch-b gives in=[] — one transient git failure leaves branch-b's pr-ready unblocked by a defect it contains. Verified in a scratch clone at a94e09c.
findings.issue: With a partly read scope (branch name read, a later Load call failed), the dedupe's !sc.Known() leg folds this branch's re-raise into another branch's row, so this branch never gets a row of its own.

findings.consequence: Docs overstate the guarantee (a transient git failure on a detached review can move rows).
findings.issue: The comment and ARCHITECTURE say the fallback refresh runs only outside a repository, but `!sc.Known() && branch == ""` also holds on a detached HEAD after a scope git failure.

findings.consequence: Extra git calls stretch the unlocked read-modify-write (#180); the comment misleads.
findings.issue: The comment says all scope git calls run before the ledger is read, but blocksHere's legacy reachability check runs inside the dedupe loop, for fingerprints this run did not even raise.

findings.consequence: A's pr-ready stops blocking on it until A's task-done re-raises it.
findings.issue: Pre-#178 Reconcile moved a row's gitHead to whichever branch last re-raised it, so an upgraded legacy row first raised on A and last on B carries B's head and reads as Orphaned on A.

findings.consequence: A revert would let a partly read scope move a branchless row off the branch it gates.
findings.issue: No test pins the `&& branch == ""` guard on the fallback refresh; the mutant dropping it survives.

pin.from: lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("- Open on other branches: %d unresolved blocker(s) in this checkout's findings ledger belong to another live branch, which they still block, or to none (merged and deleted, or outside this history), where they block nothing; none blocks this branch.", elsewhere))
